transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

Yes, it is quite normal for plastics to stay wet in dishwashers like your Bosch Serie 4. Plastic holds very little heat compared to glass or ceramic, so water droplets don't evaporate off them easily. However, if your glasses and china are also dripping with water instead of having it sheet off cleanly, that points to a drying issue rather than just the nature of plastic. The single most common cause for this is low rinse aid. Rinse aid breaks the surface tension of water so it runs off dishes in sheets rather than sitting in droplets that leave spots and wetness. It also helps with drying by allowing the water to evaporate more efficiently during the final phase. Please check your rinse aid dispenser (usually inside the door near the detergent pod holder). If it is low, top it up with liquid rinse aid. There should also be a dial or switch next to it to adjust the amount used per wash; set this to at least 6 (or the highest setting if you have very hard water). Once you have done that, run your next cycle and see if the results improve.
Just checked and the rinse aid is empty, the refill symbol is lit. I've been using all-in-one tablets though. Should I still fill it up?

Yes, you should still fill it. All-in-one tablets contain some rinse aid, but not enough for the machine's drying phase or to prevent spots in hard water areas. The refill light is on because the dedicated reservoir is empty. Please top up the rinse aid and set the adjustment dial (usually next to the cap) to at least 6. Run your next normal cycle with a full load of dishes. If the glasses sheet dry cleanly without droplets, that suggests it was just the low rinse aid level. If they are still wet or spotted, we will look at whether the wash is getting hot enough.
Ok, I'll fill it up and run a normal cycle. Do I need to change anything else, like the programme? I've been using Eco 50 every time.

You don't need to change anything else right now, but switching away from Eco 50 will likely help. Eco programmes are designed to save energy by using lower temperatures and shorter drying phases, which often leaves dishes wetter than a standard cycle would. Try running a normal or intensive programme for your next load. Also, if your Bosch Serie 4 has an 'AutoOpen' or similar feature, ensure it is enabled; otherwise, opening the door slightly at the end of the cycle lets the steam escape and helps things dry faster. Let me know how the next wash goes.
Ok, I'll try a normal programme next. I open the door straight away when it finishes though, is that okay? And I'm not sure if mine has an AutoOpen thing.

It lets the hot steam escape immediately so the dishes don't sit in condensation while they cool down. Since you're already doing that and have topped up the rinse aid, just run your next wash on a normal programme (not Eco) with a full load. The combination of rinse aid to sheet the water off, a hotter cycle to dry things better, and opening the door at the end should sort it out. If the plastic tubs are still soaking wet after that, bear in mind that plastics naturally hold less heat than glass or ceramic, so they will often remain damp even when everything else is dry. If your glasses and china come out clean and mostly dry, then the machine is working correctly - it's just the nature of plastic. Let me know how the next load comes out.
